Introduction and Brand Profile 1.1 Aim of the Project This  project  designs  and  evaluates  an  Integrated  Marketing  Communication  (IMC)  campaign  for  a selected  brand. It  follows  the  required  sequence:  Brand  and  Communication  Problem  →  Consumer Analysis  →  IMC  Objectives  →  Message  Strategy  →  IMC  Tools  →  Media  Planning  →  Implementation  → Evaluation  →  Recommendations. IMC  is  the  coordinated  use  of  advertising,  sales  promotion,  public relations,  personal  selling  and  direct  and  digital  marketing  so  that  customers  meet  one  clear,  consistent brand message wherever they come across the brand. Figure 1: The IMC Idea: Many Tools, One Consistent Brand Message Source: Group’s depiction of the IMC concept (Kotler & Keller, 2016; Belch & Belch, 2021). 1.2 Why Parle-  G? Parle-  G  is  one  of  India’s  best-  known  consumer  brands,  with  very  high  awareness  and  reach. It  is  a  strong example  for  an  IMC  study  because  its  brand  equity  is  built  on  nostalgia  and  affordability,  while  competitors are  building  new  relationships  with  young  consumers  through  premium  cookies  and  digital  media. Situation Analysis and IMC Problem 2.1 Market and Competition India’s  biscuit  market  is  led  by  three  large  players. Parle-  G  leads  by  volume  in  mass-  market  glucose biscuits,  while  Britannia  leads  by  value  in  the  overall  category  and  ITC  Sunfeast  has  grown  strongly  in premium  and  indulgent  cookies. Mondelez  (Oreo)  adds  global  sandwich-  cookie  competition. In  the segment  that  matters  for  this  campaign,  young  consumers,  rivals  mostly  speak  through  taste,  indulgence and  new  formats,  which  gives  Parle-  G  a  chance  to  own  a  different  idea:  everyday  energy  and  the  daily hustle  . 2.2 The Advertising Landscape in India India’s  advertising  industry  grew  8.3%  in  2025  to  about  ₹1,21,339  crore. Digital  now  takes  the  largest share:  ₹71,621  crore,  or  59%,  up  from  12%  in  2016  and  projected  to  reach  70%  by  2027. Television  is  still the  largest  traditional  medium  at  21%,  followed  by  print  at  14%. Within  digital,  social  media  (29%)  and online  video  (28%)  are  the  largest  formats,  and  e-  retail  platforms  account  for  about  a  quarter  of  digital spend. FMCG is the largest advertising category, with 30% of all ad spend. Source: Group’s analysis. 2.5 The IMC Problem Statement Problem:  Parle-  G  enjoys  near-  universal  awareness  and  affection,  but  much  of  its  communication  relies  on nostalgia. Among  young  consumers  (students  and  early-  career  adults),  the  brand  risks  being  remembered as  a  childhood  or  tea-  time  biscuit,  not  as  an  everyday  energy  companion  for  their  present  lives,  while rivals compete for their attention in digital and quick-  commerce spaces. Opportunity:  Link  Parle-  G’s  original  promise  of  energy  with  the  lived  reality  of  young  India’s  daily  hustle: late-  night study, interviews, long commutes and side projects. Why an integrated approach is needed •  The  audience  meets  the  brand  across  many  touchpoints:  social  media,  videos,  quick- commerce  apps,  campuses  and  the  neighbourhood  shop. IMC Objectives 4.1 Marketing versus Communication Objectives Marketing  objectives  state  what  the  business  wants  (for  example  sales,  share  or  distribution). Communication  objectives  state  what  the  communication  must  do  to  people’s  minds  and  behaviour (awareness,  understanding,  attitude,  intent),  because  communication  is  only  one  of  the  factors  behind sales. Table 8: Marketing and Communication Objectives for the Campaign Type  Objective Marketing Strengthen Parle-  G’s purchase among 18–  30-  year-  old consumers and grow its sales through quick-  commerce and general trade (target to be set against baseline sales data) Communication  Make Parle-  G the first biscuit that young consumers link with “everyday energy  for the hustle”, and move them from awareness to trial within 12 weeks Source: Group’s proposal. 4.2 DAGMAR Approach The  DAGMAR  approach  (Defining  Advertising  Goals  for  Measured  Advertising  Results)  requires  goals  that are  specific,  measurable,  tied  to  a  target  audience  and  set  for  a  time  period. It  moves  the  audience through four stages: awareness, comprehension, conviction and action. Message Strategy and Creative Concept 5.1 Positioning Positioning  statement:  For  young  Indians  chasing  their  goals,  Parle-  G  is  the  affordable,  trusted  energy boost that has been in their corner since childhood and still keeps up with their daily hustle. Findings, Business Implications and Recommendations 9.1 Key Findings 1. The  market  has  moved  to  digital. Digital  is  59%  of  India’s  ad  spend  and  FMCG brands now put 64% of budgets into it. 2. Quick-  commerce  is  a  new  communication  channel. Advertising  on  quick- commerce  grew  from  about  ₹300  crore  to  about  ₹4,000  crore  in  two  years,  and  it  sits close to purchase. 3. Parle-  G’s  equity  is  strong  but  nostalgic. The  brand  is  trusted  and  widely  available, which  is  a  strong  base;  its  communication  needs  a  present-  day  idea  for  young consumers. 4. “Hustle  ka  G”  links  the  past  and  present. It  reuses  the  brand’s  energy  promise  and the shared meaning of “G” to speak to students and early-  career adults. 5. Integration  is  the  key. Tools  are  assigned  by  journey  stage,  share  one  message  and are  timed  together,  with  64%  of  spend  in  digital  and  the  rest  in  TV,  OOH,  campus  and trade. 6. Conclusion and Limitations 10.1 Conclusion This  project  built  an  integrated  campaign  for  Parle-  G  step  by  step,  from  the  brand  problem  to  the evaluation  plan. The  central  finding  is  that  Parle-  G  does  not  need  to  change  what  it  stands  for. It  needs  to be  heard  in  today’s  language,  in  the  places  where  young  people  spend  their  time. “Hustle  ka  G”  does  this by  linking  the  brand’s  energy  promise  to  the  daily  hustle  of  young  India,  delivered  through  a  digital-  led  but fully  integrated  mix  of  advertising,  sales  promotion,  public  relations,  digital  and  experiential  tools. A  clear schedule,  a  budget  logic  that  follows  the  audience,  and  a  measurement  plan  tied  to  DAGMAR  objectives make the campaign practical and accountable. 10.2 Limitations •  The  campaign  is  a  proposal.
